gloss: to continue; to occur in succession; to be consecutive

definitions.gloss: to continue; to occur in succession; to be consecutive
definitions.explanation: For events, actions, or things to follow one after another without interruption. Emphasizes the unbroken sequence or series nature of occurrences.

examples.japanese: {事故|じこ}が{連続|れんぞく}して{起|お}きた。
{三日|みっか}{連続|れんぞく}で{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}っている。
examples.english: It has been raining for three days in a row.

examples.japanese: あのチームは{五年|ごねん}{連続|れんぞく}で{優勝|ゆうしょう}しているから、{今年|ことし}も{期待|きたい}されている。
examples.english: That team has won the championship five years in a row, so they're expected to do well this year too.

notes:
Often used as a noun modifier: {連続|れんぞく}＋counter (e.g., {三日|みっか}{連続|れんぞく} — three days running). Very common in news and sports contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ～{日|にち}{連続|れんぞく} — ~ days in a row
- {連続|れんぞく}{殺人|さつじん} — serial murder
- {連続|れんぞく}ドラマ — serial drama, TV series
- {連続|れんぞく}{記録|きろく} — consecutive record
- {連続|れんぞく}{優勝|ゆうしょう} — consecutive championships

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {続|つづ}く — to continue (general, everyday); focuses on duration rather than sequence
- {継続|けいぞく}する — to continue, maintain; emphasizes sustained effort or ongoing state
- {相次|あいつ}ぐ — to occur one after another; emphasizes that similar events keep happening (often negative events)
